small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs with BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_P=4/8 and BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_P=32 (num_warps=8, num_stages=3) — the conv-GEMM has OC=64 and IC*KH*KW=72 reduction, so wider OC tiles per program reduce weight-load redundancy across the grid.
- The weights are tiny (64*8*9 = 4608 floats); preload the entire weight tensor into shared memory once per program (or hoist the weight gather outside the kw loop and use tl.load with cached vector loads) to eliminate redundant weight reads across the IC/KH/KW loop.
- Try reordering loops so KH/KW are outer and IC is inner with static_range on IC (IC=8 is small and constexpr-friendly) — this lets Triton unroll the full 72-iter MAC chain and better hide latency; also test num_stages=4 with BLOCK_P=8.
large_guidance:
- Switch to an explicit im2col-style GEMM tile where the K dimension (IC*KH*KW = 72) is contiguous: pack input gather into a [BLOCK_P*POOL*POOL, K] tile loaded once per program, and use tl.dot against a [K, BLOCK_OC] weight tile. With K=72 padded to 128 and BLOCK_M=256 (=BLOCK_P*16 outputs pre-pool), this uses tensor cores instead of the current outer-product accumulation in fp32 scalar MACs.
- Make the kernel persistent over N and the pool-spatial axis: each program handles a full (OC_tile, multiple pool tiles) and streams pool tiles, amortizing weight loads (load weights into SRAM once per program). With OC=64 fitting entirely in one tile, one program per (N, pool-tile-group) can keep weights resident.
- Consider channels_last input layout (NHWC) so the IC dimension is contiguous and the K-axis loads in im2col become a single coalesced vector load per spatial position, instead of the current strided per-(kh,kw) gather across IH*IW planes.
